accessor/class-accessor-pair.description: A class getter and setter pair; the setter stores a function that a method calls back through the getter.

accessor/getter-returns-function.description: A getter returns a function that the caller invokes; the getter itself runs on the property load.

argument-flow/parameter-and-return.description: Function values flow into parameters of a `const` arrow and a method, and out through returns.

argument-flow/rest-and-spread.description: A rest parameter collects function values and a spread argument fills parameters.

await/awaited-function.description: An async function resolves to a function value; the caller awaits it and calls the result.

await/promise-resolve-value.description: A value wrapped by `Promise.resolve` and an object property read after `await`.

block-function/catch-and-finally.description: In a sloppy-mode CommonJS module, functions declared inside a `catch` block, a `finally` block and an `if` nested in a `try` are called after their blocks.

block-function/try-and-if.description: In a sloppy-mode CommonJS module, functions declared inside a `try` block, an `if` block and an `else` block are called after the block, from the enclosing function.

call-apply-bind/bind.description: `bind` makes a function that forwards to its target with a fixed `this` and leading arguments.

callback/builtin-invoked.description: Functions passed to Array methods and to an inline arrow are invoked by the runtime, not by user code.

callback/higher-order-parameter.description: A user-written higher-order function calls the function it receives as a parameter.

callback/nested-higher-order.description: A callback passed through two user functions before a builtin calls it.

cjs-exports-property/exports-of-factory-.description: `exports.x` holds a function returned by a factory call; another module requires and calls it.

cjs-exports-property/function-expression.description: Function expressions are assigned to exports.x and call each other through the exports object.

cjs-exports-property/renamed-destructuri.description: Declared functions are attached to exports.x and required through a destructuring pattern that renames one of them.

cjs-interop/compiled-default.description: TypeScript-compiled CommonJS: `exports.default`, `__esModule`, an interop helper and `(0, m.default)(...)`.

cjs-interop/define-property-export.description: `Object.defineProperty(exports, name, { get })` exports, read through `require` and called.

cjs-module-exports/function-with-propert.description: module.exports is replaced by a function, and a helper is attached as a property of that function.

cjs-module-exports/object-literal.description: A CommonJS module assigns an object literal to module.exports; callers require it whole and destructured.

class-features/class-expression.description: A class expression returned from a factory and extended; the subclass inherits its constructor.

class-features/fields-statics-super.description: Instance fields, a static method, `extends`, `super(...)` and `super.m()`.

class-method/instance-and-static.description: A TypeScript class with a constructor, an instance method calling another through this, and a static factory.

class-method/subclass-override.description: A subclass overrides a method that the base class calls through this, and calls the base implementation through super.

closure/captured-callback.description: A closure stores a callback in a captured variable and calls it later from a separate returned method.

closure/captured-parameter.description: A closure in a property descriptor calls a parameter of the function that created it.

closure/factory-returned-function.description: A factory returns an inner function that captures a variable and a helper; callers invoke the returned function.

computed-key-foldable/const-key-literal.description: Object literal keys and member reads use `const` names and a template literal without substitutions.

computed-key-foldable/constant-concatena.description: A computed key folds to a constant: string concatenation and a `const` string.

computed-key-unknown/escaped-object.description: A computed key reads an object the module exports, so code outside may add fields; no complete answer is right.

computed-key-unknown/known-literal-table.description: A key computed at run time selects from a literal whose fields are all known; the answer is every field, left open.

constant-key-field/private-field.description: A class keeps a function in a private field and calls it from a method.

constant-key-field/string-and-numeric-ke.description: Functions stored under string and numeric literal keys, and a store into a parameter object, are called back through the same keys.

destructuring/array-and-nested.description: Functions reach calls through array destructuring, a nested pattern, a default and an array rest.

destructuring/object-defaults-and-rest.description: Functions reach calls through object destructuring with a default, a rename and a rest element.

dynamic-import/computed-specifier.description: import() receives a specifier assembled at run time, so the loaded module and the called function are hidden.

dynamic-import/literal-specifier.description: A module is loaded with import() of a string literal and a function from the loaded namespace is called.

dynamic-property/computed-key-known-set.description: Methods are called through computed keys taken from a constant list in the same file.

dynamic-property/key-from-input.description: A method is called through a key read from the environment, so the target is not visible in the source.

esm-namespace/namespace-object.description: A namespace import used as an object: passed to a function and read with a member.

esm-namespace/star-and-live-binding.description: `export *` through two barrels and a live binding reassigned by the exporting module.

esm-reexport/named-barrel.description: An index module re-exports named functions from two modules; the caller imports through the barrel.

esm-reexport/star-and-alias.description: A barrel uses export * for one module and an aliased re-export for another function with the same local name.

eval/direct-eval.description: Direct eval runs a string that calls a function in scope; the call exists only inside the string.

eval/function-constructor.description: new Function builds a function from a string; the built function calls a callback passed to it.

exported-initializer/cjs-exports.description: A CommonJS module assigns `exports.x` and `module.exports.y` from calls at module level, one call nested in another's argument.

exported-initializer/esm-declarators.description: An ES module exports several declarators of one `export const` and an `export default` expression, each initialised by a call.

function-object/factory-made-constructor.description: A factory defines a function, attaches an `init` property and returns it; the result is exported and called through.

function-object/own-properties.description: A function carries functions as own properties, written by assignment and by `Object.defineProperty`.

iteration/for-of-array.description: `for…of` over an array of functions and over an array filled with `push`.

iteration/generator.description: A generator yields function values that a `for…of` loop and spread consume.

literal-spread/object-spread.description: Methods reach a call through object spread and array spread of a literal.

literal-spread/override-after-spread.description: A later property overrides one copied by spread, and an array literal spreads another literal.

logical-join/conditional-callee.description: The callee itself is a conditional, a guarded `cb && cb()` and a comma expression whose last operand is a parameter.

logical-join/default-operand.description: A function value reaches a call through `||`, `??`, `&&`, `?:` and the comma operator.

module-initializer/arrow-in-initializer.description: An exported constant is built by a factory call that receives an arrow function, which calls a helper; the factory returns a wrapper.

module-initializer/chained-call.description: An exported constant is initialized by a chained call a().b().c() through builder objects.

module-initializer/class-expression.description: An exported constant holds a class expression whose methods call a module function and each other through this.

module-initializer/exported-call.description: An exported module-level constant is initialized by a call whose argument is another call.

module-initializer/local-initializer.description: Non-exported module-level constants are initialized by nested calls and by an object whose arrow property calls a function.

module-initializer/object-literal-method.description: An exported object literal holds methods that call module functions and each other.

new-and-prototype/constructor-function.description: `new` on a function value: the instance's prototype is the function's `prototype`, `this` is the instance.

new-and-prototype/return-override.description: A constructor returns an object, which replaces the instance; a factory returns the constructor that `new` is applied to.

object-of-functions/literal-methods.description: An object literal holds shorthand methods and arrow-function properties that call one another through the object.

object-of-functions/registry-built-later.description: An empty object is filled with function properties after creation and passed to another function that calls through it.

object-of-functions/registry-passed-arou.description: A registry object of functions is passed to a function that calls one of its members.

optional-chaining/optional-call.description: `a?.b()` and `f?.()` call the same functions as the non-optional forms.

optional-chaining/optional-member-chain.description: An optional chain through two members, with one path that short-circuits on `undefined`.

package-vendor/cjs-require.description: A CommonJS package requires a nested vendored module `vendor/util/index.js` and calls its exported functions through the required object.

package-vendor/esm-import.description: A package ships its vendored dependency under `vendor/`; the package's module calls a function the vendored module exports.

promise/async-await.description: An async function awaits other async functions and an async arrow stored in a constant.

promise/then-chain.description: Named functions are passed to then and catch on a promise chain and run as reactions.

prototype-chain/escaped-subclass-instanc.description: An exported instance of a subclass calls a method found two links up its prototype chain, through `this` and from outside.

prototype-chain/object-create.description: `Object.create(p)` makes an object whose methods come from `p`, and a prototype chain of two links.

prototype-chain/set-prototype-of.description: `Object.setPrototypeOf` and a prototype replaced by a literal.

prototype/constructor-function.description: A constructor function gets methods on its prototype; an instance created with new calls them.

prototype/escaped-instance.description: An exported factory returns an instance to outside code; its method calls a sibling method the instance inherits from its prototype.

prototype/inherited-method.description: Object.create links a child prototype to a parent; the child instance calls a method found only on the parent prototype.

returned-function/branch-returns.description: A function returns a declared function, a closure or its parameter from different branches; the caller invokes the result.

returned-function/conditional-default.description: Functions return a conditional expression, an `||` default or a `??` default between a parameter and a declared function; callers invoke the result.

returned-function/stored-in-property.description: The result of a function that returns one of several functions from different branches is stored in a property and called through it.

returned-function/two-levels.description: A parameter is reassigned to the result of a function that forwards another function's branch returns, then called.

same-name-member/cjs-static-method.description: A CommonJS module function calls an anonymous static method of the same name on a constructor stored in a variable; the member call reaches the method.

same-name-member/wrapper-of-static-metho.description: A module function forwards to a static method of the same name on a constructor function; the member call reaches the method, not the function that shares its name.

sequence-callee/compiled-interop.description: Compiled CommonJS calls an imported default export through `(0, _m.default)(a)` after `_interopRequireDefault(require(...))`, and a named export through `(0, _m.name)(a)`.

sequence-callee/local-sequence.description: An ES module calls a local function and an object method through `(0, f)(a)`, the nested `(0, (0, f))(a)` and `(0, m.g)(a)`.

this-forms/literal-method-this.description: `this` in a method of an object literal, an arrow's lexical `this` and a method stored and called through another object.

this-forms/union-receiver.description: A method stores an arrow into `this`; a parameter that may hold either of two instances calls the stored function.

unary-iife/umd-prologue.description: A minified UMD prologue: a function under `!` is called with the module factory, which declares three inner functions; one function per line so each carries a label.

unary-iife/unary-operators.description: Function expressions called under `!`, `void`, `+` and `typeof` at module level; each body calls a module function.

decisions: Construct edges are identified by (file, line of the call expression's start, callee label); labels cannot express how many sites on one line call the same callee, so precision is counted per (line, callee).
When one line labels a callee both as a direct call and as a callback, the callback counts as found only when a second distinct call site on that line reaches it.
Predicted edges to functions without an @fn label are counted apart and are neither true nor false positives.

A labelled hidden path (@unknown) is 'reported-unknown' when a call site on that line carries an unresolved marker, 'false-complete' when it has resolved targets and no marker, and 'silent' when polint has no call site there or one with neither. For the refined column the refined layer's own status decides; sites it has no row for keep the base layer's marker.

A labelled call line is false-complete when polint resolves a call site on it to labelled functions that miss a labelled `@calls` callee and no call site on the line carries an unresolved marker. Lines are the unit of the labels, so on a line with several call sites the targets and markers of all of them count together.
A base edge whose target is an import binding rather than a function is a miss, counted as 'stops at import binding'.

Observed package edges are mapped to polint by exact call-expression span (falling back to the polint call site in the same file ending at the same byte) and by callee span (the same span, else the innermost polint function in the same file ending at the same byte that does not start inside the observed span).
Observed edges whose site or callee has no polint counterpart stay in the denominator: recall is over every observed edge.
Export accuracy compares exported names per file; star re-export rows and the CommonJS whole-value `module.exports` row carry no name and are left out of the export-fact names but counted by status.
Refined edges are counted when they carry a target function, whatever their status.
Polint models a class as one function spanning the class body and has no separate constructor function, so a `Class.constructor` label and an observed constructor callee map to the class function.

Observed implicit edges (accessors, coercions, iterator protocol) have a position but no call expression; they are reported by kind but left out of the headline package recall, which is over calls and callbacks.

A package is analysed as the package it is: its `analysed` globs are the include set (a construct case includes all its files), and of polint's default excludes only `**/node_modules/**` and `**/.git/**` apply, so a package's own `vendor/` is analysed; observed edges touching an excluded file count as 'site or callee in a file polint does not analyse'.
Missing call sites and functions are not worked around: a function or call polint does not extract counts as a miss.

An observed callee maps to the polint function with the same span before the innermost one ending at the same byte: a concise arrow returning an arrow, `(a) => (b) => ...`, ends at the same byte as the arrow it returns.

Every missed observed edge is attributed to one gap from a syntax census: Oxc's own function and call spans with their syntactic context, parsed again apart from the analysis. A site or callee polint does not extract is charged to the outermost function around it that polint does not extract, else to the outermost enclosing function or the call in a gap; edges polint maps go to constructors, callbacks to built-ins, computed keys and prototype or class methods, in that order. A computed-key miss is counted whether or not the key set is known, so that row is an upper bound for computed keys over a known set.
A census function counts as extracted when polint has a function in the same file ending at the same byte, or, for a class constructor, when polint has the class.
Every package edge with other targets and no unresolved marker is kept as an example; other outcomes and gaps keep a bounded sample, in observed-edge order.

Process peak RSS is measured with `wait4` like the matrix runner does. Linux carries the parent's resident size into the child's peak at fork, so every process is launched before the report loads any fact dump, and the launcher's own peak is recorded with the cost section. The in-process analysis peak has no such floor.
Each fact dump has a wall-clock limit (`--dump-timeout`, 600 s by default); a tree whose dump exceeds it is reported as timed out for that plan and has no scores in that column.

A package with `dump_budget_s` in `inputs.toml` has a time budget for each of its fact dumps; the report is written either way, and the run exits with status 1 naming every dump that ran over its budget or timed out.

deviations: Jelly has no tiers and no notion of a complete answer or of a heuristic edge, so every Jelly edge counts as claimed, its edges to external callbacks included. Its wrong-target counts are an upper bound and are not comparable with polint's exact tier.
Jelly's per-file module entries are left out of callee matching, as polint's `module` functions are.
Jelly is given the same shipped source files polint analyses, as entry files; `-b <package>` makes its paths relative to the package root.
Jelly models `_interopRequireDefault` and similar helpers natively instead of analysing their bodies; polint analyses the helper as code. On async this alone accounts for most of Jelly's misses.
polint's outcome classes ("stops at import binding", "marked unresolved") have no counterpart in Jelly's output.
Wall time is the docker wall time of one run, container start included, on the machine that recorded the committed outputs; it is not measured with polint's cost runs.
ACG (js-callgraph) is not run: its parser rejects ES2020 and drops such files silently, so it cannot analyse these packages.
